key_insight: SPG-Layout improves text-driven 3D indoor scene synthesis by combining statistical object priors with a hierarchical, large-object-first layout strategy to better handle non-Manhattan geometry.
engineering_relevance: The method is relevant for robotics, digital twins, and interior design tools that need physically plausible scene generation in irregular indoor spaces.
method: Use statistical priors of object distributions to guide training and improve environmental understanding.
Place large objects first in a hierarchical layout pipeline to reduce downstream conflicts and violations.
Optimize jointly for semantic realism and physical plausibility in non-orthogonal environments.
evidence_signal: The authors introduce a new benchmark of 500 diverse non-Manhattan environments and report consistent gains over prior methods in both Manhattan and non-Manhattan settings.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of the learned priors and the new benchmark may not fully capture all real-world non-Manhattan layouts.
paper_title: Text-Driven 3D Indoor Scene Synthesis in Non-Manhattan Environments
